svg.title: Protocol errors and tool execution errors, and where each one ends up
svg.desc: Two columns. On the left, a protocol error: triggered by an unknown method, a missing _meta key, or arguments the schema rejects, it travels as a JSON-RPC error object with a numeric code and no result member, is marked as not always arriving with HTTP status 200, and a dashed arrow leads to a box saying the client handles it and the model never sees it. On the right, a tool execution error: triggered by a missing row, a timeout, or a departure date in the past, it travels as a successful HTTP 200 result whose isError field is true, and a solid arrow leads to a box saying it is fed back to the model so it can correct and retry. A closing line gives the rule that separates them: a request that breaks the shape of CallToolRequest belongs on the left, and a well-formed request this tool cannot satisfy belongs on the right.
svg.text: A tool that fails is not a protocol error
Only one of these is a JSON-RPC error. The other is a successful response reporting failed work.
The server could not act on the request at all.
Unknown method, missing _meta, arguments the schema rejects
The request was fine. The work failed.
Row not found, timeout, a departure date in the past
so it can correct and retry
Send the reason, not just the word "failed".
A model can only fix what it can read.
A request that breaks the shape of CallToolRequest is on the left. A well-formed request this tool cannot satisfy is on the right.
